clue.text: What —— a novel insect!

definitions.meaning: the blank completes the title of an 1872 children's novel by Susan Coolidge about a girl's growing up
a large green North American grasshopper named for its call

explanation.walkthrough: The dash is a gap to fill: the two words that complete the novel's title, run together, also name an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: What Katy Did is a classic girls' novel, and the run-together name is also a long-horned grasshopper whose song seems to repeat those words.

clue.text: Like a problem Alexander solved at a stroke

definitions.text: Like a problem Alexander solved at a stroke

parts.words: Like a problem Alexander solved at a stroke
parts.note: Alexander the Great cut the Gordian knot with his sword instead of untying it

explanation.definitionFit: Intricate or hard to solve, from tangled rope, and Alexander's problem was literally a tangled rope.

clue.text: One who can't stand up to a day's journey?

definitions.text: One who can't stand up to a day's journey?

parts.words: One who can't stand up to a day's journey?
parts.note: seems to describe someone too frail for travel, but means one who stumbles and falls, and also an excursionist on a day out

explanation.definitionFit: Someone making a short pleasure excursion, and also anyone who stumbles.

clue.text: Composer fellow, we hear, is a nude painter

parts.note: a don is a college fellow

indicators.note: says the following words are to be taken as spoken

parts.note: 'is Etty': William Etty was an English painter famous for his nudes

explanation.surface: A gossipy claim that some composer is a painter of nudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'is Etty' into the sound of IZETTI; William Etty (1787-1849) painted nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was the Italian composer of Lucia di Lammermoor and other operas.

clue.text: Put frantic call round to the joint, management

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a hasty phone call to the place running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is only a link; 'joint' is an adjective (shared), not a noun for a place or a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people sharing the controls of a vehicle or system, so the management of it is shared.

clue.text: Sound way to beat a racing-dog?

indicators.note: placed first, this word says the following phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to beat something you might whip it, the command 'whip it'

explanation.surface: A question about how best to drive on a greyhound-like dog in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (a sound way) but signals a homophone: 'whip it' said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A small slender dog bred from greyhounds and terriers and raced on tracks.

clue.text: Is past the point like

parts.note: W, west, is a point of the compass
as means like

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark that something is beyond the point of resemblance.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of 'is' is the simple past form of to be.

clue.text: Mean, to put motorway up the Strand!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the motorway's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: M1, the motorway from London to Leeds
a ply is a strand of rope or yarn

explanation.surface: Someone means to build a motorway along London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but here it is a ply of yarn. 'up' turns M1 into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest or signify something without stating it outright.

clue.text: Magazine section put in train a new departure?

definitions.meaning: a detachable insert in a magazine

definitions.text: put in train a new departure?
definitions.meaning: a train starting its journey is said to ...

explanation.definitionFit: A removable supplement in a magazine; a train leaving the station also does this.

clue.text: No rough way to offer even parts in play

parts.note: to tender is to offer

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters are taken, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Advice to be gentle when offering lines in a theatrical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even parts in' takes the second and fourth letters of 'play', L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gently and lovingly is the opposite of doing it roughly.

clue.text: Easterners like Chesterton's tea

definitions.meaning: people from Asia, in older usage
G. K. Chesterton wrote 'Tea, although an Oriental, / Is a gentleman at least'

explanation.definitionFit: Asians were once called by this word, and Chesterton's poem calls tea one of them.

clue.text: Powerful supporter only maybe soft in the head

indicators.note: at the head means the soft letter goes at the very front of the word

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word only could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A strong backer who is perhaps a little soft-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges ONLY into YLON; 'in the head' puts P at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel tower holding up high-voltage power lines, so a supporter of power in a literal sense.

clue.text: Highest extremities, literally, of New Jerusalem's ninth foundation

parts.note: the highest point is the top
the extremities of the alphabet, taken letter by letter, are A and Z

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding description of the outermost tips of a holy city's foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' means the extremities are letters: the alphabet runs from A to Z. In Revelation 21 the New Jerusalem's wall has twelve jewelled foundations, the ninth this gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation 21:20 lists the gemstones of the holy city's foundations, the ninth being a yellow gem.

clue.text: Snug quarters for the Fox family?

definitions.text: Snug quarters for the Fox family?

parts.words: Snug quarters for the Fox family?
parts.note: a small cosy room or nook, read whimsically as a burrow where young foxes, called cubs, live

explanation.definitionFit: A small snug space or compartment, and split up it suggests a den for fox cubs.

clue.text: Army coat we prepare for battle round the West

indicators.note: round here sets the west beside the arming, just ahead of it

parts.note: we, the people of Britain, from the British setter's view
W is the abbreviation for west
to arm is to prepare for battle

explanation.surface: Britons readying for war wrap up in army greatcoats around the western front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is loose: W simply comes before ARM. A British warm is a short thick overcoat worn by army officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A short heavy overcoat worn by British army officers, especially in the First World War.

clue.text: Alloy suitable for the main : ruler's spear?

definitions.meaning: a silvery tin-based metal mixture used for tableware

definitions.text: suitable for the main : ruler's spear?
definitions.meaning: the figure who 'rules the waves' (the main, the sea) carries a trident, which would be made of her own metal

explanation.definitionFit: A pewter-like tin, antimony and copper alloy, named after the female personification of Britain who rules the sea in the song.

clue.text: Realm most unlikely to be in a whirl

indicators.note: unlikely says the words realm most come out in an improbable order

explanation.surface: A kingdom is hardly ever thrown into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful whirlpool, hence any violent swirl of water or turmoil.

clue.text: In which Will put up his sword, refusing to strike?

definitions.text: In which Will put up his sword, refusing to strike?

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
the Bard is William Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A swordsman sheathes his blade rather than attack.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put up' a sword is to sheathe it, and a sheathed sword does not strike, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheath for a sword, where it is put away when not in use.

clue.text: Trouble with soaring price re postage by them

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about the cost of postage rising steeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble with' rearranges SOARING PRICE RE, fourteen letters. The definition is loose: these birds carried messages, so post went by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing birds were used to carry messages, so mail was sent by means of them.

clue.text: Not acting with the others in Greek capital

parts.note: the rest are the others

indicators.note: the capital letter of a word is its initial, here the first letter of Greek

explanation.surface: Someone not performing with fellow actors in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek capital' suggests Athens, but it is just Greek's first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-of-work actors are said to be resting between jobs.

clue.text: Like the ceremony which no single principal left

definitions.text: Like the ceremony which no single principal left

parts.words: Like the ceremony which no single principal left
parts.note: a wedding, after which neither of its two main figures walks away unmarried

explanation.definitionFit: Relating to marriage or the wedding service, after which both bride and groom are no longer single.

clue.text: They may involve a shift in one's beliefs

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle or roll up, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: Religions may require one to change one's convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Religions or creeds, systems of belief.

clue.text: " Do good ——, and blush to find it fame " (Pope)

definitions.text: Do good ——, and blush to find it fame

parts.words: Do good ——, and blush to find it fame
parts.note: a line from Alexander Pope's Epilogue to the Satires; the gap is filled by a phrase meaning secretly

explanation.definitionFit: The missing phrase means secretly or covertly, which is how Pope's modest benefactor does good.

clue.text: Not the all-American girl

indicators.note: not the whole of the word, the italic all stressing that only part is taken

explanation.surface: A girl who is not the classic all-American type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the all' means take only part of 'all-American': its letters ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, also the botanical name of heather.

clue.text: A pie's turned brown

indicators.note: turned over, the letters of the pie are put in a different order

parts.note: taken with its S as written

explanation.surface: A pie left too long in the oven has gone brown.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown colour, as in old photographs, from the ink of the cuttlefish.

parts.words: This plea is out of place
parts.note: a defence that the accused was elsewhere; the Latin word itself means 'elsewhere', so the plea is that one was not at the place

parts.note: reads like a parliament adjourned during a revolt, but describes seats hanging from a cable that carry skiers up a slope
